reads.summary:
DECISION: The tracker can be a drop card, but it cannot work with NO server change. Crews could send ticks today. They could never read each other's ticks back, so "everyone sees the same shared progress" is impossible on v5.87.

WHAT WORKS TODAY (no change):
- An editor POSTs the tracker HTML to /api/cards (edit link only, lines 2761-2818). The card is about 26 KB of mock-up plus 13 KB of data, far under MAX_CARD of 2 MB (line 138).
- The server mints the token (cardToken, line 154). Re-posting with the same token updates the HTML and keeps the same link (line 2776), so printed QR sheets survive a fix.
- "QR codes one per sheet" needs nothing from the server. Each sheet's QR can be /d/<token>#area=N. The route matches the pathname only (line 2568), the fragment never reaches the server, and the one hash-pinned inline script can read location.hash.
- Ticks can go as legacy reports to POST /d/<token>/report (lines 2526-2565). They must be note-only: fields only take delivered/in_position/installed/levelled/stairs (line 208). The card must be made with keys [], because each report copies card.keys (line 530) and the page files reports into every listed reference's drawer (reportsFor / reportedCard in build/GC500_v10.60p1).
- The main page on the edit link can read them with /api/reports?token= (lines 2745-2760).

WHAT IS MISSING: There is no card-scoped read anywhere.
- The only /d/ routes are POST report/scoped (line 2460), POST report (line 2526) and the HTML (line 2568). A GET to /d/<t>/report falls through to the 404 at line 2944.
- /api/cards and /api/reports need the edit link (lines 2738, 2746). The edit key must never go on a phone.
- Scoped replies (v5.63) are not a way round it. A card allows at most 40 targets (lines 363, 2803) against 75 rows. Fields are delivery/demob only (lines 271-274). The card needs expires and a typed `by` (lines 356, 362). And nothing reads scoped_reports.json at all: no GET exists, and /api/reports reads only `reports`.
- The only no-server-change way to share progress is an edit page re-posting the card HTML all night with the ticks baked in, while phones reload. I rule it out: each post rewrites cards.json, and each reload is an 'open' write plus a log line (lines 2581-2583).

SMALLEST SAFE ADDITION (next free server number after checking the board; Codex claimed v5.88 at STATUS.md line 2076). About 70 lines in the v5.63 "own store" style:
1. FILES (line 69): add `ticks: path.join(DATA_DIR,'tracker_ticks.json')`.
2. After line 218, in the server's style:
   - a comment headed "THE SERVICING TRACKER READS ITS OWN TICKS BACK" with Andrew's words, saying a tick is somebody's word in its own store and never touches the record, a delivery, a charge, the card reports or their pruning;
   - `const MAX_TICK_BODY=4*1024, MAX_TICKS_PER_CARD=6000, TICK_ROW_RE=/^[A-Za-z0-9?_.-]{1,16}$/, TICK_ID_RE=/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{7,63}$/;`
   - `let ticks = loadStore(FILES.ticks,'tracker ticks',null,plainObject) || {};`
   - `function persistTicks(){ try{ writeWhole(FILES.ticks,ticks); return null; }catch(e){ console.error('ticks',e.message); return e; } }`
3. POST /api/cards (after line 2803): an opt-in `tracker:{rows,days}` built only from the editor's body. Rows are de-duplicated, filtered with TICK_ROW_RE and !protoKey, at most 400. Days use the handler's own `day` regex, at most 7. It becomes null unless both lists are non-empty. Every driver card stays exactly as it is.
4. New route `/^\/d\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\/ticks$/`, placed before line 2566:
   - Unknown token: wrongKey 404 (counted). No tracker: 404 (a right key, not counted). Expired: 410.
   - GET: returns this card's ticks, filtered by `?since=` with `t.at >= since` (the phone de-duplicates by id). The projection is id, row, day, done, at, tapped_at, name_given. No open is counted, nothing is saved and no log line is written.
   - POST: body bounded to 4 KB, `{ticks:[1..20]}`. Each tick needs a phone-made id, a row in the card's rows, a day in its days, and done true or false. The same id with the same content counts as `already`; the same id with different content is 409.
   - Each row stores `at` (server time), `tapped_at` (the phone's clock, labelled as the phone's), name_given (up to 80 characters) and verified:false.
   - The per-card cap answers 507. The save is write-then-rename, rolled back and answered 507 if it fails, and logged as logWrite 'tracker ticks' or 'tracker ticks NOT SAVED'. The answer is `{saved, already, at}`.
5. GET /api/ticks?token=&since= (beside line 2745): edit link only, like the reports, because a tick carries a typed name. It uses a hasOwnProperty guard and returns the title, expired and tracker for each token. Letting the view link see the ticks without names is Andrew's call.
6. Optional: a tick count in cardBrief (line 161) and on /health. Bump BUILD (line 41) and /health build (line 2405).

The card script then posts ticks to /d/<t>/ticks and polls GET with since. It works out the 08:00-08:00 AEST day, the percentages and each area's finish time (its last tick) itself. The server never reads the record.

ABSOLUTE MINIMUM ALTERNATIVE (about 15 lines): an opt-in GET /d/<t>/report read-back over the existing reports store, with no photos or pins. It works, but I advise against it for the reasons under risks.

facts.fact: Card store: MAX_CARD 2 MB (one card, HTML with inline pictures); KEEP_CARDS 400; CARD_TOKEN_RE /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,64}$/; cards loaded via loadStore with no snapshot fallback (a damaged cards.json refuses start).

writeWhole = writeFileSync to file.tmp.<pid> then renameSync (whole or nothing, NO fsync); persistCards/persistReports/persistScoped return the error instead of throwing. The record itself is fsynced (saveRecordFile).
cardToken = crypto.randomBytes(24).toString('base64url') (32 chars). The server mints it; POST /api/cards reuses body.token only if that card already exists, so re-posting keeps the same link/QR.

cardExpired: expired only if c.expires is set and qldDay() > expires (Brisbane day, UTC+10). expires null = never expires. Event nights Thu 22 to Mon 26 Oct 2026, so expires '2026-10-26' covers the Sunday-night window (ends 08:00 Mon 26).
cardBrief strips html and adds bytes, opens count, last_open, expired, reports count and last_report.
pruneCards: only when over 400 cards, deletes the oldest EXPIRED cards only (single-argument cardExpired fix, v5.58).

GET /d/<token> serves c.html with this CSP: "default-src 'none'; img-src data: blob:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src data:; script-src '<sha256 of first <script>>'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'" plus X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy no-referrer, nosniff, Cache-Control no-store.

Only ONE inline script runs: cardScriptHash hashes the first bare <script>...</script> (no attributes). Inline on*= handlers, a second script, type=module/defer scripts and external scripts are all blocked. The mock-up has exactly one bare <script> and no on*= handlers. Its Google Fonts <link> will be blocked (it falls back to system fonts). Navigate links to google.com/maps still work as top-level navigation, and no-referrer keeps the card token from leaking.

Every GET /d/<token> records an open: c.opens appended (last 200 kept), persistCards() rewrites all of cards.json synchronously (error ignored), and logWrite 'card open' writes token, load and title. So polling the card HTML would be a write each time.

The card runs on the same origin as the main /e/ and /v/ page, so localStorage is shared with the main page. The tracker should use its own key prefix. There is no offline service worker (CSP plus no-store), so the tracker needs its own localStorage outbox and must not reload itself.

POST /d/<token>/report (legacy): unknown token gives wrongKey 404 (counted); expired gives 410; body up to MAX_REPORT 6 MB; must be a JSON object; empty answer gives 400; dedupe by id family plus reportIdentity; pruneReports; write-then-answer (507 and in-memory rollback on failure); logWrite 'card report' with token, load, by_name_given, field names, photo count, pin flag.

cleanReport allowed fields: id (up to 64 chars, else random), name_given (up to 80), fields only delivered/in_position/installed/levelled/stairs with answers yes/not yet/not applicable, note (trimmed, up to 1200), up to 6 photos as data:image/(jpeg|png|webp) base64, pin lat/lon/accuracy_m/how. Also stamps token, load, keys = card.keys (up to 40), at = server time, source 'reported on the drop card', verified false.

reportIdentity hashes fields, note, pin, name_given and photos; it excludes at and id. A same-id resend with identical content returns already:true. A same id with different content is kept as id.<rand> with retry_of.

pruneReports: KEEP_REPORTS 4000 rows in total. Only runs when over 4000, and deletes whole report sets of EXPIRED cards, oldest card first. A live card never loses reports. There is no per-card cap and no hard total cap. Withdrawn cards' reports are never pruned (cards[k] is missing).

Capacity: about 300 ticks a night x 4 nights = 1,200 rows (about 1,500 with unticks), roughly 260-330 bytes each as legacy reports, so about 0.4-0.5 MB. That fits under KEEP_REPORTS 4000. Live /health (GET, read only) shows 7 cards, 0 live, so existing report volume is small.
facts.where: server.js line 207; GET https://gc500-production.up.railway.app/health (cards 7, cards_live 0, build v5.87, record 9704)

facts.fact: POST /d/<token>/report/scoped (v5.63): body up to 16 KB. prepareReport is run against cardGrant built from the stored card: allowedKeys = c.targets, or c.keys at unitKey null. validateServerGrant needs 1-40 targets, an absolute expiry (c.expires) and a non-empty createdBy (c.by), and checks revocation and expiry. Report shape: submissionId, phase (delivery or demob), target (must be in the grant), fields (phase fields only), photoIds (always refused today: canUseFile requires files[id].card === token, which nothing sets), pin, note (up to 1200 chars, no data:), nameGiven. Stored in scoped_reports.json with fingerprint and retryDecision (409 on changed content).
Scoped replies are WRITE-ONLY today. No route reads scoped_reports.json: /api/reports reads only `reports`, and the live page build has zero occurrences of 'report/scoped'.

Scoped cannot cover the tracker on one card: 75 rows exceed the 40-target limit. Card POST also drops keys/targets that fail REF_RE /^[A-Z0-9?_.-]{1,12}$/, and areas13.json's 'Spare' row fails it. One card per area would fit (at most 9 refs per area), but there is still no read-back.
No card-scoped read exists. /d/ routes are only POST report/scoped, POST report and the HTML (any method). GET /d/<t>/report falls to the 404 'Nothing here.' page (not counted as a wrong key).
GET /api/cards: edit only (403 for view). Returns all cards via cardBrief, newest first.

GET /api/reports: edit only (403 for view). Optional ?token=. Returns each card's load, title, run_date, card_withdrawn, expired and full report rows INCLUDING photo data URIs, plus cards_with_reports and total. JSON is not compressed by send().

The live page polls GET /api/reports with NO token filter every 20 s while visible (REPORTS_EVERY_MS = 20000; loadReports). It files rows by r.keys into reference drawers labelled 'somebody's word, not a Coates record' and says they change no light, date or figure. Nothing applies a report to the record.
/api access: level() takes the token from the x-gc500-token header or ?t=; edit or view or null. A wrong key on /api is counted only if one was presented.

Wrong-key limiter: 30 wrong tokens in 5 min per X-Real-IP gives 429 on EVERY keyed path (including right keys and /d/) until the oldest miss is 5 min old. Unknown card tokens are counted on all three /d/ routes. Right tokens, expired cards (410), /health, / and /p/ are never counted. There is NO rate limit on traffic with a correct card token.

Write log: logWrite appends JSON lines to writes.log asynchronously (not served over HTTP; the admin page names it). Card lines carry the card token in plain text ('card made/updated/withdrawn' with by, 'card open', 'card report', 'scoped report', and the NOT SAVED variants). The edit key is never logged, and the console error path redacts /d/<token>.

POST /api/cards stores token, load (60), title (160), run_date, expires (yyyy-mm-dd), contact {name 80, phone 30}, html, keys (REF_RE, 40), targets (40), created (kept on update), updated, by (from the x-gc500-who header, 80), opens (kept). It rejects over 2 MB by Content-Length first (413), runs pruneCards, persists with rollback (507), and logs. No tracker-type field exists.
The expired-card page says 'This drop card has expired ... It stopped working the day after the run' (drop-card wording, cosmetic for a tracker). The 'Ring' line comes from c.contact.

Server v5.88 is CLAIMED by Codex (2 Oct 2026, DRAFT, not deployed). The live server boots from a volume blob named by SERVER_FILE with rollback in SERVER_FILE_KEEP, so the deploy needs a blob PUT, a Railway variable change and a redeploy, on Andrew's 'Upload'.

reads.constraints:
- Card HTML: at most 2 MB (MAX_CARD, line 138).
- Exactly one bare inline <script>, hash-pinned. No inline handlers, no external CSS, fonts or scripts. Images only as data: or blob:. connect-src 'self' only (lines 2590-2592).
- Cache-Control no-store and no service worker, so no offline load.
- Each GET of the card HTML writes an open (cards.json rewrite plus a log line, lines 2581-2583), so the card must not poll its own HTML.
- Expiry is a Brisbane day (qldDay, line 159). Set expires '2026-10-26' or later for Thu 22 to Mon 26 Oct 08:00. After it, POST answers 410 and the HTML is a 410 page.
- Legacy report: body at most 6 MB, note at most 1200 chars, name at most 80, id at most 64, at most 6 photos, fixed delivery fields only (lines 206-209, 508-537). Reports are pruned only above 4000 rows, expired cards first (lines 207, 220-228).
- Scoped: body at most 16 KB, at most 40 targets per card, delivery/demob fields only, needs card expires and by, photos always refused, and no read route at all.
- Wrong-key limiter: 30 misses per 5 min per IP locks every keyed path for that IP (lines 2362-2383). The tracker outbox must treat 404 and 410 as final and never retry them.
- Stores are written whole on every write (synchronous, tmp plus rename, no fsync). A damaged store with no snapshot (cards, reports, scoped; a new ticks store the same) refuses service start (lines 82-85, 109-113).
- The edit key never goes in a card, a QR or a log. The card token opens only its card (line 132).
- No server version is free until claimed on STATUS.md (Codex holds v5.88). Deploying goes through the SERVER_FILE blob and needs Andrew's yes.
reads.risks:
1. Ticks as legacy reports (the no-change write path) bloat the edit page's 20-second /api/reports poll. The poll takes everything, uncompressed, with no token filter. By the last night that is about 0.3-0.5 MB extra per poll, roughly 55-90 MB an hour on Andrew's phone while the page is visible.
2. Legacy ticks share the 4000-row pruning. Once the total passes 4000, pruning deletes whole expired cards oldest first, so tracker volume could evict old drivers' delivery evidence (photos, pins). That is low today (7 cards) but structural.
3. Every legacy tick rewrites all of reports.json synchronously, including every driver photo data URI.
4. The legacy endpoint accepts 6 MB bodies from anyone holding a QR sheet, and no correct-token rate limit exists, so a disk can be filled. A dedicated tick route at 4 KB with a per-card cap closes this.
5. If the tracker card is made with keys, every tick appears in up to 40 references' drawers as a drop-card report. If fields like installed:'yes' were used as ticks, they would read as delivery/install claims. Use keys [] and note-only, or the separate store.
6. A tracker outbox that retries a withdrawn or unknown token gets 404s that are counted. 30 in 5 minutes locks that phone's public IP (shared under carrier NAT) out of every link, including the edit link, for up to 5 minutes.
7. A read-back route must never call persistCards or logWrite. Six phones polling for four nights is about 100k requests.
8. Opt-in per card is essential. A blanket GET /d/<t>/report would newly expose drivers' typed names, photos and positions to anyone holding a driver card.
9. writeWhole has no fsync, so a power cut right after the answer could drop the last tick (a process crash cannot).
10. A new store loaded with no snapshot fallback stops the whole service from starting if its file is damaged (the existing pattern). Consider passing a snapshot prefix.
11. Version clash: server v5.88 is claimed by Codex (draft). There is also a page-era folder named v5.88_v5.89_hotfixes, so a name for the next server number can be confused with it.
12. Typed names are attribution, not identity (verified:false). The view link cannot see ticks unless Andrew chooses to open a nameless projection.
13. tapped_at is the phone's clock. Server `at` is the honest time; offline-queued ticks arrive late, so the card should send its chosen service day explicitly rather than let the server work it out.

reads.summary:
Read-only research of the live page /home/user/fish/03_GC500_Delivery_Control/build/GC500_v10.60p1/GC500_Delivery_Control_hosted.html, checked against server.js v5.87 where the page relies on it. Nothing was edited, deployed or written. No secrets were printed.

MAKING A CARD. Two page features make cards today, and both go through SYNC.backend.makeCard, which POSTs to /api/cards (lines 54545-54549):
(a) makeDropCard(id), lines 39233-39268. It needs a name (whoAmI) and builds the html with cardHtmlFor(l) (39615-39732). The body it posts is {token, load, run_date, expires = addDays(run date, 1), title, keys, contact {name, phone} of the lead, html}. It then writes keep.card {token, url, at, by, expires} into S.loads[id] (39261-39264), so a drop card DOES write the job record.
(b) daily821Send, around lines 47010-47030. Its payload is {load:'installer-day:'+iso, run_date, expires, title, keys (no more than 40), html}, with a 1.9 MB guard (47027-47028). It has no reply form. Its edit gate is daily821Editable (46957).

The card html is one self-contained page. The reply form is cardReportSection(as) (39903-39963) and the card's only script is cardReportScript() (39966-40111). That script POSTs to location.pathname + '/report' (40080). The script is put in as a bare <script> tag, written `<${'scr'+'ipt'}>` (39730), because the server hashes the first <script>…</script> for the card's CSP (server.js 175-178). The QR code comes from qrSvg(text, cell) (39426-39433). cardMadeDialog (39436-39478) shows the link, a QR at cell 4, a text panel and Withdraw (withdrawCard 54552).

READING REPORTS BACK. SYNC.backend.reports() does GET /api/reports (54556-54558). loadReports() (39745-39783) puts them into a global REPORTS {by_key, by_load, total, error, forbidden}, kept apart from S. On a view link it is skipped before any fetch (39748-39752). Polling: reportsPoll() runs every REPORTS_EVERY_MS = 20000 ms (39794-39822), only while the page is visible. It is started from the record pull (54465), which itself runs every 4 s (54488). A 403 is remembered and not asked again (39801). After each poll it refreshes only an open reference drawer (39812-39813). No tab is redrawn.

SHOWING REPORTS. The only place reports appear is reportedCard(key) (39847-39888). It is rendered at the top of a reference's drawer (35632) and labelled 'Reported from the drop card … somebody's word, not a Coates record … changes no light, no date and no figure'. reportedState/reportChip (39828-39846) take the latest answer per field. No figure, light or charge reads REPORTS.
- SYNC.backend.cards() (GET /api/cards, 54550) exists but nothing calls it.
- The page never calls /d/<token>/report/scoped. The server has no GET for scoped replies, and /api/reports returns only the legacy store (server.js 2745-2759).

EVENT NIGHTS TAB. The tab is ['nights','Event nights'] (15014), its pane is <section id="pane-nights"> (11745), and it is drawn by renderPass → renderNights1022() (57527). The code is the v10.22 IIFE in <script id="nights1022-script"> (87996-88246), exported as window.Nights1022 / renderNights1022 (88243-88245).
- NIGHTS covers only Fri 23, Sat 24 and Sun 25 Oct (88005-88008). defaultNight changes over at 06:00 (88078-88083), not 08:00.
- render() (88085-88131) replaces the whole pane.innerHTML (88104).
- The tab's ticks DO write the shared record: Nights1022.write puts kind 'nights1022' docs into S.loads (88052-88064).
- nights1040 and servicing748 (27790-27855) are the servicing cost and charge lines used by Costs and P&L. They are not the run sheet. The tracker must not touch them.

EDIT LINK OR VIEW LINK. restBackend() (54394-54402) matches /e/ or /v/ in the path and stores the token as gc500.edit or gc500.view in localStorage. tok() prefers the edit token. Every request sends the header x-gc500-token. pull() asks /api/version and sets SYNC.level and SYNC.readonly from v.level (54426-54436). The link's own claim is in claims (54502-54503) and is copied into SYNC.claims at 54339. The gates are capability() (57579-57601), canEdit, mayWrite(what) (57608-57614) and applyCapability() (57616-57650). On a view link applyCapability disables every input that is not marked data-ro.

HOW A SERVICING TRACKER CARD COULD WORK.
1. Make it from the Event nights tab with SYNC.backend.makeCard, on the edit link only, using a gate like daily821Editable. Make one card per area, so each printed sheet carries one QR code, as Andrew asked. Suggested body: {load:'servicing:<areaId>' (60 characters at most), run_date:'2026-10-22', expires:'2026-10-26', title, keys: [] (see the risks), contact, html with one bare inline script}.
2. Do not save the token into S.loads the way makeDropCard does. Find the cards again later through the unused backend.cards() (/api/cards returns the token and load in cardBrief), so making the cards writes nothing to the record.
3. Ticks cannot travel on the existing /report. The server keeps only the five delivery fields, answered yes, not yet or not applicable (server.js 208-209, 509-515). The note is cut at 1200 characters and the name at 80. A small server addition is needed, for example POST /d/<token>/tick plus GET /d/<token>/progress, so every phone sees the same progress. The card's CSP already allows this: connect-src 'self' (server.js 2589-2592).
4. A view-level read is also needed, because /api/reports is edit-only.
5. On the page, show progress read-only in a separate container on pane-nights, added after Nights1022.render, with buttons marked data-ro. Fill it from REPORTS.by_load filtered by 'servicing:', or from a new backend method on the same 20 s beat. Redraw only that container, never call render(), so a field being typed in on the run sheet is not wiped.

facts.fact: SYNC.backend.makeCard POSTs the card JSON to /api/cards with the x-gc500-token header and throws 'this link can view but not make drop cards' on a 403. The next methods in the same object are cards() (GET /api/cards, never called anywhere) and withdrawCard(token) (DELETE /api/cards/<token>).

SYNC.backend.reports() does GET /api/reports (cache no-store) and throws 'this link can view the record but not the card reports' on a 403. The comment says it is read only and writes nothing to the record.

makeDropCard(id) needs whoAmI() and a paired load. It builds the html with cardHtmlFor(l), sets expires = addDays(l.date, 1) and contact = the TEAM lead {name, phone}, and calls makeCard with {token (to remake), load, run_date, expires, title, keys, contact, html}. It then writes keep.card {token, url: location.origin + r.url, at, by, expires} into S.loads[id] with stampIt('loads', id); save(); bump(). That is a write to the job record.
On the file edition, with no service, makeDropCard opens the card html in a new window instead.

cardHtmlFor(l) returns a complete <!doctype html> page: inline CSS, inline images as data URLs, a Navigate button (navUrl), one tel: link, the reply form ${cardReportSection(as)} at line 39724, and one bare script written <${'scr'+'ipt'}>${cardReportScript()}<${'/scr'+'ipt'}> at line 39730.

cardReportSection(as) is the reply form. It has radio questions delivered, in_position, installed, levelled and stairs (the last three only where the rate card offers that line), plus name, note, up to 6 photos and a location.

cardReportScript() is the card's only script. It shrinks photos, takes a geolocation pin, makes a snapshot ID so a retry is not counted twice, and POSTs JSON to location.pathname.replace(/\/$/,'')+'/report'. It reads nothing back.

The second card maker is daily821Send. Its payload is {load:'installer-day:'+iso, run_date, expires: addDays(iso,1), title, keys (refused above 40), html}, refused above 1,900,000 bytes, and posted through daily821Publish → SYNC.backend.makeCard with a 30 s timeout. daily821CardUrl only accepts a same-origin /d/<token> address. The edit gate daily821Editable() checks capability()==='edit', not readonly, status live, makeCard present and the record fully synced.

qrSvg(text, cell) draws a QR code with the bundled qrcode() at level M, with a 4-module quiet zone, as scalable SVG. cardMadeDialog uses qrSvg(card.url, 4) and has Copy, Open, a text panel (smsPanel) and Withdraw.

REPORTS is kept apart from S: {tried, at, by_key, by_load, total, error}. loadReports() returns forbidden at once when SYNC.claims==='view', so no fetch is made. Otherwise it calls SYNC.backend.reports() and indexes every report row by r.load (by_load) and by each of r.keys (by_key), newest first. After a passing failure it keeps the last good data.

Polling: REPORTS_EVERY_MS = 20000. reportsPoll() uses setTimeout, skips while document.hidden, stops for good when forbidden, and after each read only refreshes an open reference drawer (window.Idle1006.refreshDrawer). A visibilitychange listener restarts it.
reportsPoll() is started from inside the record pull(), after a successful /api/state. pull itself runs every 4000 ms while the page is visible, and on focus.

Reports are shown only by reportedCard(key) at the top of a reference drawer. It says 'Reported from the drop card', 'somebody's word, not a Coates record', 'Nobody at Coates has checked any of this… It changes no light, no date and no figure'. reportsFor, reportedState and reportChip use REPORT_FIELD_WORDS.
The page never calls /d/<token>/report/scoped. No page code reads scoped replies.

Event nights tab: the tab list has ['nights','Event nights'], the pane is <section class="pane" id="pane-nights">, and renderPass dispatches state.tab==='nights' to renderNights1022(). The print route is #print/nights/<iso>.
The Nights1022 IIFE (v10.22) has KIND 'nights1022' and PREFIX 'nights1022/'. NIGHTS are 2026-10-23 Friday, 2026-10-24 Saturday and 2026-10-25 Sunday (final). There is no Thursday.

Nights1022 functions: unitRows (WC units in number order), key, rec, night, write (writes S.loads[PREFIX+iso+'/'+part+'/'+id] through mayWrite, whoAmI, stampIt, save, bump), nightRecords, summary, defaultNight (06:00 AEST changeover), render (pane.innerHTML replaced at 88104), filesHtml, bind, sheetHtml, print. It exports window.Nights1022 and window.renderNights1022. No other code touches pane-nights.

nights1040 and servicing748 are the servicing COST and charge lines (servicing748base1040, nights1040, nightRates1040, servicing748, servicing748Total). Costs and P&L, the toilet branch and the charges all use them. They are not the run sheet and a tracker must never feed them.

restBackend(): DATA.edition must be 'hosted'. The path regex /^\/(v|e)\/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/ stores the token in localStorage as gc500.edit or gc500.view. tok() prefers gc500.edit, so a phone that ever opened the edit link keeps using the edit token. headers() sends x-gc500-token and x-gc500-who (S.operator).

Server: the legacy report keeps only fields delivered, in_position, installed, levelled and stairs, with answers yes, not yet or not applicable. The note is cut at 1200 characters, the name at 80, keys at 40. The server stamps 'at' itself and marks every row source 'reported on the drop card', verified:false. MAX_REPORT is 6 MB and KEEP_REPORTS is 4000.

Server: /d/<token> serves the stored html under the CSP "default-src 'none'; img-src data: blob:; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; font-src data:; script-src '<sha256 of first <script>>'; connect-src 'self'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'". An expired card answers 410. There is no GET for reports by card token.

Server: GET /api/cards and GET /api/reports are edit-level only, so a view link gets 403. /api/reports accepts ?token= (the page does not use it) and returns only the legacy reports store, not the scoped one. POST /api/cards is edit-level, the card is no more than 2 MB (MAX_CARD), expires and run_date must be yyyy-mm-dd, load is cut at 60 characters and title at 160, and keys are filtered by REF_RE and cut at 40.

reads.constraints:
Card size: no more than 2 MB (server MAX_CARD). The daily card guards at 1.9 MB on the page (47028).

CSP on a card page: no external scripts, styles, fonts or images (only inline, data: and blob:). Exactly one bare <script> tag, because only the first one is hashed. connect-src 'self' (only its own service). form-action 'none', so posting goes through fetch. The page writes the tag as <${'scr'+'ipt'}> so its own outer script is not broken.

Card fields: expires is a yyyy-mm-dd day, and the card answers 410 and refuses reports once the Brisbane day is past it. For Thu 22 08:00 to Mon 26 08:00 use expires '2026-10-26'. load is no more than 60 characters, title no more than 160, keys no more than 40 matching REF_RE, contact name no more than 80 and phone no more than 30. KEEP_CARDS = 400 (only expired cards are pruned). KEEP_REPORTS = 4000, shared with drop-card reports.

Legacy reports: only the five delivery fields are stored, with answers yes, not yet or not applicable. The note is no more than 1200 characters and the name no more than 80. 'at' is server time. Up to 6 photos as data URLs.

Reading back: /api/reports and /api/cards are edit-link only. The page skips reports outright when SYNC.claims==='view'. Reports poll every 20 s only while the tab is visible, and the record every 4 s. A card page has no read endpoint today.

Event nights tab: render() replaces the whole pane, so any live progress must go in its own container. Buttons must carry data-ro to stay usable on view links. The tracker must never call Nights1022.write or write S, S.loads, nights1040 or servicing748.

Days: Andrew's tracker days run 08:00 to 08:00 Gold Coast time (UTC+10), Thu 22 to Mon 26 Oct. The run sheet's NIGHTS are Fri 23 to Sun 25 with a 06:00 changeover, so a separate day list is needed, with Thursday marked 'if needed'.

Never print or log the edit key. The QR codes must hold the card URL /d/<token>, never /e/.

reads.summary:
How server releases are built, tested and shipped, and the safe path for a new server (v5.88 or v5.89) with rollback.

FIRST, A NUMBERING CLASH: Codex already claimed server v5.88 ("shared-record reliability") on 2 Oct (STATUS.md:2076). It is marked "DRAFT, not ready or deployed". I found no v5.88 server files on any branch fetched here. git commit c0ac787e is the old PAGE v5.88, not the server. So before starting: fetch codex/gc500-current-release-03oct, read PR #1, and either get Codex to release the number or claim v5.89 on STATUS.md (AGENTS.md:56-58).

HOW SERVER RELEASES ARE BUILT. A Python patch is applied to the exact live server.js. It refuses to run unless the input's SHA-256 is the live one, and each replacement must match exactly once (patch_server_v587.py:20-32). It writes a new server.js, then `node --check` and record the bytes and SHA. The page toolchain (build.sh, upload_page.py) handles only the PAGE: upload_page.py POSTs /api/admin/app. There is no server deploy script in the toolchain.

HOW THEY ARE TESTED (local only). Each server folder has a node test that does the following:
- spawns `process.execPath server.js` with a throw-away DATA_DIR from mkdtemp
- uses fake VIEW/EDIT tokens (16-128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-], and different) on a free 127.0.0.1 port
- points CLICKSEND_BASE at a pretend ClickSend server
- polls /health until the server is up, then sends requests with the x-gc500-token header
- stops it with SIGTERM and reads the start-up banner from server.log

I ran it in this environment (Node v22.22.0, TMPDIR set to the scratchpad): 14/14 pass. The repo copy of server.js hashes to d5a0d777…, which is the live v5.87.

HOW THEY GO LIVE. The server file lives on the Railway volume as a content-addressed machine blob. The start command copies $DATA_DIR/machine/blobs/$SERVER_FILE to /app/server.js and runs `exec node /app/server.js`. If that blob is missing, it falls back to the stale SERVER_B64 server (v5.78).

STEPS TO SHIP THE NEW SERVER SAFELY:
1. Claim the number on STATUS.md and push the claim.
2. Write patch_server_v588.py in a server_v5.88_<what>_DRAFT/ folder.
   - Guard on the base SHA d5a0d777da4871af1bf88804b4ef223354a29c2560213ab56f7897445b398fdc.
   - Bump both labels: `build: 'v5.87'` (server.js:2405) and `const BUILD = 'server v5.87` (server.js:41). v5.85 forgot the banner (STATUS.md:2628).
   - Keep protectedBlobs/SERVER_FILE_KEEP and the SIGTERM flush intact.
   - Put any new state in a NEW store file, so v5.87 can ignore it on rollback.
3. Test locally:
   - New tests for the new routes, following test_mms_sender.js.
   - Copies of the earlier suites placed beside the new server.js, since they all spawn path.join(__dirname,'server.js'): v5.87 test_mms_sender.js (14, with the label check changed to v5.88), v5.86 test_delivery.js (45) and v5.85 test_mms.js (37).
   - Prove there is no record write: /api/version stays unchanged and records.json is untouched.
   - Rehearse the boot swap locally (blob → SERVER_FILE → restart → roll back), as in v5.84 TESTS.md:256-303. rehearse_deploy.sh itself is not in the repo.
4. Push the DRAFT with hash and test results, get a review (recommended), and mark READY TO UPLOAD with the exact source commit.
5. Pre-flight, read only:
   - Confirm edit access: GET /api/version must return level 'edit' (the upload_page.py --dry-run logic).
   - GET /api/export with the edit key, and keep the copy privately.
   - Note /health's version.
   - Note the Railway variables: SERVER_FILE (expected d5a0d777…), SERVER_FILE_KEEP (f5b9a3f7…, 76afbd99…, 264363…, b8d38b…), MMS_FROM=shared, RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.
6. Stage the blob: PUT /api/admin/machine/blob/<sha> with the raw bytes. The server checks the hash before writing. Then GET /api/admin/machine and confirm both the new and v5.87 blobs are listed. Do NOT import or register a machine set until the redeploy is done: the live v5.87 deletes every blob not named in the set or in SERVER_FILE/SERVER_FILE_KEEP, and the env only changes on redeploy.
7. One Railway change, with Andrew's yes:
   - SERVER_FILE=<new sha>
   - SERVER_FILE_KEEP = d5a0d777… plus every existing entry
   - keep MMS_FROM, add any new variables
   - one redeploy (about a 10 s gap, single volume), in a quiet window before Thursday 22 Oct night
8. Verify:
   - The deploy log says `server from volume blob <sha>` and `sha256sum /app/server.js` equals the new sha.
   - The banner's first line names the new version, says 'server blob N kept off the public set', and has no '!!! RECOVERED FROM SNAPSHOT'.
   - /health shows the new build, ok:true, record_recovered:null and the same record version.
   - The view page bytes are unchanged; the new routes are checked by GET only.
9. Rollback: set SERVER_FILE back to d5a0d777da4871af1bf88804b4ef223354a29c2560213ab56f7897445b398fdc, keep the new sha in SERVER_FILE_KEEP, and redeploy. /health should then show v5.87.
   - If the banner shows v5.87 after the deploy, SERVER_FILE has a typo. If it shows an old server, it booted the SERVER_B64 fallback: roll back at once.
   - If the log says 'REFUSING TO START', do not roll back blindly (DEPLOY.md:174-183).
10. Record it: README with the LIVE time, rename the folder _LIVE, add a STATUS.md row, commit, push, and note it on PR #1.

facts.fact: Server v5.88 is already CLAIMED by Codex (2 Oct 2026, 'shared-record reliability', DRAFT, not ready or deployed). Coordinate on PR #1, or take v5.89, before using the number.
No server v5.88 files were found in any branch git can see here. Commit c0ac787e 'GC500 v5.88 and v5.89 hotfixes' is the old PAGE versioning (v5.88_v5.89_hotfixes/patch_v588.py), not the server.

The live server source in the repo is 237,432 bytes, SHA-256 d5a0d777da4871af1bf88804b4ef223354a29c2560213ab56f7897445b398fdc (verified locally just now; matches the README and STATUS). node --check passes.

Patch pattern: the base SHA-256 guard refuses another base or a second application; the local rep() requires each replacement to match exactly once; the usage line is `python3 patch_server_v587.py <base server.js> <out server.js>`.
Version labels to bump in a new server: the /health field `build: 'v5.87'` and the banner `const BUILD = 'server v5.87 ...'`. v5.85 forgot to bump the banner.
facts.where: server.js:2405 and server.js:41 (v5.87 folder); STATUS.md:2628 (banner lesson)

facts.fact: Local test harness: spawns process.execPath on path.join(__dirname,'server.js') with env {PATH, PORT (free port), DATA_DIR=fs.mkdtempSync(os.tmpdir()), VIEW_TOKEN, EDIT_TOKEN, CLICKSEND_* pretend values, CLICKSEND_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:<fake>/v3, PUBLIC_BASE}. It polls /health up to 100x100 ms, sends x-gc500-token header requests, stops with SIGTERM and reads the banner from DATA_DIR/server.log.
Ran here: `TMPDIR=<scratchpad> node test_mms_sender.js` gives 14/14 on Node v22.22.0. The temp data dirs landed in the scratchpad; no network to live.
Token rules the local server enforces at start: VIEW_TOKEN and EDIT_TOKEN must be 16-128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-] and different, or it exits.
CLICKSEND_BASE (the pretend provider) is honoured only when NODE_ENV is not 'production'. Do not set NODE_ENV=production in local tests.

Regression suites that can be rerun against a new server by copying them beside its server.js (each spawns __dirname/server.js): v5.86 test_delivery.js (45 checks), v5.85 test_mms.js (37), v5.87 test_mms_sender.js (14; its 'health says v5.87' check needs the label changed).
The v5.84 broad suite (49 checks) is NOT portable: it hardcodes /tmp/claude-0/stage/server, a scratchpad kit page and port 8815, and needs a seeded data/ folder.

A deploy/rollback rehearsal was done for v5.84 using the start command's logic locally: blob upload, then SERVER_FILE switch and restart, then rollback, then roll forward. rehearse_deploy.sh itself is not in the repo; only its output is.

Start command: copies $DATA_DIR/machine/blobs/$SERVER_FILE to /app/server.js if it exists and is non-empty, otherwise decodes SERVER_B64 (an older server), then runs `exec node /app/server.js` as PID 1. The literal current command text is not in the repo; read it from the Railway service config.

Blob staging route: PUT /api/admin/machine/blob/<sha256> (edit level). The bytes' hash is checked before writing, a blob already present is acknowledged without a rewrite, max 48 MB. GET /api/admin/machine (edit) lists the blobs on the volume.

Registering a machine set deletes every blob not named in the set and not in protectedBlobs(). protectedBlobs() reads SERVER_FILE and SERVER_FILE_KEEP from process.env, so a newly staged blob is unprotected until a redeploy with the variables set. Do not run machine imports (admin page 'Import the machine' or machine_set.py) between staging and redeploy.

The v5.87 go-live recipe: Codex staged blob d5a0d777 on the volume; Claude set MMS_FROM=shared, SERVER_FILE=d5a0d777…, SERVER_FILE_KEEP=f5b9a3f7…,76afbd99…,264363…,b8d38b… (every earlier entry kept); one redeploy (deployment 81618338… SUCCESS). The deploy log showed 'server from volume blob d5a0d777…' and `sha256sum /app/server.js` = the same hash; /health build v5.87, record version unchanged.
Rollback recipe: set SERVER_FILE back to the previous hash (keeping the new one in SERVER_FILE_KEEP) and redeploy. Railway's own Rollback should also work, but the variable route is explicit.
Do not roll back blindly when the log says 'GC500 REFUSING TO START': that is a damaged store, and an older server could start empty over it.
Redeploy downtime is a gap of seconds (about 10 s measured for v5.85) because a service with a volume cannot run two deployments at once.

SIGTERM handler: flushes the record and the log, then exits; the hard limit is 8 s. DEPLOY.md recommended RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS=10 (Railway's default is 0). Whether it is set on the service now is not recorded.

Things to check after start: the banner line (version, record version, drop cards, 'server blob N kept off the public set', any '!!! RECOVERED FROM SNAPSHOT') and /health {ok, version, cards, cards_live, machine, record_recovered, build}.
Edit access check without writing: GET /api/version returns level. upload_page.py stops unless level=='edit' and passes the key to curl on stdin (-H @-), so it never appears in argv.

On 14 Oct, Claude's credential proxy injected a wrong x-gc500-token, giving 401 on every /api call. Later entries the same day show uploads succeeded. Re-prove edit access by dry run before staging a blob.

Pre-deploy backup: `curl -H x-gc500-token… $BASE/api/export -o …` (edit level). Keep it out of git.

Process rules: claim a version on STATUS.md and push before starting; a DRAFT folder with README; READY TO UPLOAD names the exact source commit; risky changes wait for Andrew's yes; tests only read live (GET); the edit key never goes in files, logs or messages.

Drop card facts relevant to a tracker route: MAX_CARD 2 MB; KEEP_CARDS 400; expires is a yyyy-mm-dd Queensland day, and a card counts as expired once today's date is after it; POST /api/cards (edit) can re-post to an existing token (keeps created and opens).

The card page CSP allows only the hash of the FIRST bare <script> block, plus connect-src 'self', img-src data: blob:, no external hosts, form-action none, frame-ancestors none. A QR library and QR images must therefore be inline or data: URIs.

reads.constraints:
- Version number: v5.88 is claimed by Codex (STATUS.md:2076). Coordinate, or use v5.89.
- Staging order: the new blob must be staged with PUT /api/admin/machine/blob/<sha> before the Railway change. No machine-set import is allowed between staging and the end of the redeploy, or v5.87 deletes the unprotected blob (server.js:1308-1309).
- Variables:
  - SERVER_FILE_KEEP must keep d5a0d777… (v5.87) plus the existing f5b9a3f7…, 76afbd99…, 264363… and b8d38b….
  - MMS_FROM=shared must stay set.
  - SERVER_B64 must be left alone: it is a stale v5.78 fallback, and a v5.84+ server is too large for one variable (DEPLOY.md:199-201).
- What the new server must keep: protectedBlobs() and the SIGTERM flush (8 s hard exit). New state goes in a separate store file written whole (atomic temp file then rename), answering 507 on a disk failure, so that v5.87 ignores it on rollback. records.json, cards.json, reports and scoped_reports formats must not change.
- Deploy window: one redeploy means a gap of about 10 s on a single volume. Pick a quiet window before the Thursday 22 Oct "just in case" night; the event is 23-25 Oct.
- Tests:
  - Local only: 127.0.0.1, fake tokens of 16-128 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_-] that differ, DATA_DIR from mkdtemp (set TMPDIR to the scratchpad), a pretend ClickSend (NODE_ENV not production).
  - Stop only the processes you spawned, by PID.
  - Checks against live are GET only.
- Secrets: the edit key only ever comes from the GC500_EDIT_TOKEN environment variable or the host credential proxy, sent through curl's stdin header. It never goes in argv, files, logs or messages.
- Card limits a tracker must respect:
  - 2 MB html per card, at most 400 cards kept.
  - Expiry is a Queensland day (yyyy-mm-dd), so the expiry for the Sunday-to-Monday 8am night should be the Monday or later.
  - CSP: one hashed inline script, connect-src 'self', data:/blob: images only.
  - The wrong-token limiter returns 429 by IP after repeated bad tokens (server.js:2377-2412).
reads.risks:
1. Version clash: two agents shipping different "server v5.88" builds would break the handover rules. Codex's claim is a month old, but it is still on the board.

2. Blob loss: the staged blob is not protected until the redeploy has happened. If anyone imports a machine set before then (admin page or machine_set.py), live v5.87 deletes it. The redeploy then boots v5.87, or worse, the stale SERVER_B64 (v5.78) if SERVER_FILE names a missing blob. v5.78 lacks the v5.84 hardening, including snapshot recovery and refusing to start empty. Check the deploy log's sha256sum every time.

3. A typo in SERVER_FILE gives the same fallback; the banner and /health build field reveal it.

4. Polling load: if the tracker reads progress back through GET /d/<token>, every poll from every phone rewrites the whole cards.json (up to 400 cards at up to 2 MB each) and appends a log line. A v5.88 read-back route must not call persistCards or logWrite per request, and should answer from memory.

5. Shared mobile addresses: phones behind one carrier address that hit a withdrawn or expired token could trip the wrong-key limiter (429) for each other.

6. Edit access: Claude's credential proxy failed with a wrong x-gc500-token on 14 Oct (STATUS.md:213). If not re-verified with a dry run, staging can fail partway.

7. Rollback safety: rolling back is safe only if v5.88 adds new files and leaves the existing store formats alone. A store v5.87 cannot read would make it refuse to start, or with older servers start empty.

8. Unverified on the live side: the literal start command and the current values of RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS, SERVER_FILE_KEEP and NODE_ENV were not read from Railway (read-only research, no Railway calls made). Confirm them in pre-flight.

9. Missing harnesses: the v5.84 49-check suite and rehearse_deploy.sh are not runnable from the repo as-is (hardcoded /tmp staging paths; the script is not committed). A new rehearsal script is needed to repeat the boot-swap test.

spec.approach:
DECISION: one drop card is the servicing tracker. It has one secret token and opts in with `tracker:{rows,days}`. There are 14 printed sheets, one per area (13 areas plus "No location yet"). Each sheet's QR is the same card link with the area number after a #: `/d/<token>#a1` … `#a13`, and `#a0`. On the server, server v5.89 adds a small store of its own for ticks and three routes. Nothing else changes.

WHY THIS ONE (checked in v5.87 server.js, sha256 d5a0d777…, which is the live build; live /health on 18 Oct 05:23 AEST reads build v5.87, record 9704, 7 cards, 0 live):
- What it reuses from drop cards, unchanged:
  - The server mints the token (cardToken, line 154).
  - Re-posting the same token keeps the link (line 2776), so printed sheets survive a fix.
  - The card is frozen HTML under a hash-pinned CSP: one bare <script>, `connect-src 'self'` (lines 174-178, 2590-2600).
  - Expiry is a Queensland day (qldDay and cardExpired, lines 159-160).
  - Edit-only making and listing (lines 2737-2740, 2761-2818), the opens log, and the withdraw route.
- The # part never reaches the server. The /d/ route matches only the pathname (line 2568). I checked this in headless Chromium against a prototype server: the script saw `#a5`, and writes.log never did.
- Andrew's words are "Qr codes one per sheet" and "When scanned it automatically goes to set day". The QR therefore names only the area. The card picks the 08:00-to-08:00 day from server time, so the same QR works on all four days.
- One token means one shared tick list:
  - every phone sees every area and the overall percentage;
  - a crew can help in another area;
  - one re-post fixes all 14 sheets.

WHY A SERVER CHANGE IS UNAVOIDABLE. A card page cannot read anything back today.
- The only /d/ routes are POST report/scoped (line 2460), POST report (line 2526) and the HTML (line 2568). A GET to /d/<t>/report falls to the plain 404 (line 2944).
- /api/reports and /api/cards are edit-only (lines 2738, 2746), and the edit key must never go on a phone.
- So without a change, phones could send ticks but could never see each other's. That fails "Each section will automatically update" for several phones.

REJECTED:
1. Ticks as legacy reports (no server change). Phones cannot read them back. They would also:
   - only fit as notes (REPORT_FIELDS, line 208);
   - add load to the page's 20 s /api/reports poll, which fetches every report row, photos included, with no token filter;
   - share the KEEP_REPORTS 4000 pruning (lines 207, 220-228);
   - accept 6 MB bodies from anyone holding a sheet.
2. Scoped replies (v5.63). A card takes at most 40 targets, and there are 75 rows. Fields are delivery or demob only. Nothing reads scoped_reports.json back.
3. An editor re-posting the card HTML all night with the ticks written into it, while phones reload. Every reload is an open, a whole rewrite of cards.json and a log line (lines 2581-2583).
4. One card per area (14 tokens). Overall progress would need 14 reads, crews could not see other areas, there would be 14 re-posts per fix and 14 entries in cards.json.
5. A brand-new /s/<token> namespace. It would duplicate the minting, CSP, expiry, listing and withdraw that drop cards already have.
6. Ticks in the job record (the way Nights1022 writes S.loads). That is the job record: Andrew said it must never tick, charge or change delivery states, and phones would need the edit key.

PROVEN IN A SCRATCHPAD PROTOTYPE (not in the repo, nothing deployed): the patch below is 87 added lines on the v5.87 base (244,483 bytes, node --check OK).
- Local smoke test: 52/52.
- Earlier suites against the prototype: v5.87 test_mms_sender 14/14 and v5.86 test_delivery 45/45 (label checks changed to v5.89); v5.85 test_mms 36/37, the one fail being its build-label check.
- A Chromium CSP check passed: the card script read and posted its own ticks; an external fetch was blocked; localStorage worked; offline fetch rejected cleanly.
- Prototype files:
  - /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fish/b3d08fad-688f-5986-9fd9-2f1442b3bb1a/scratchpad/svc589/patch_proto.py
  - /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fish/b3d08fad-688f-5986-9fd9-2f1442b3bb1a/scratchpad/svc589/smoke.js

WHAT IT IS. The card's HTML, made by the main page (see main_page) and served at /d/<token> under the existing card CSP (lines 2590-2600). It is about 35 KB against the 2 MB MAX_CARD (line 138). It is the mock-up (servicing_tracker_DRAFT/mockup.html) made real, with these changes:
- a full document: `<!doctype html>`, `<meta charset>`, `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1,viewport-fit=cover">` and `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`;
- the Google Fonts links removed, because the CSP blocks them and the CSS already falls back to Arial Narrow / Arial;
- the "Mock-up" label removed;
- exactly ONE bare `<script>` at the end of body, because cardScriptHash pins the first `<script>…</script>` (lines 174-178). The AREAS data is written with `<` escaped as <, and there are no inline on*= handlers.

The data is the 14 groups from areas13.json: 75 rows, 257 units, each with ref, qty, types, asset nos, where, drop and pin. The card shows:
- how many units are at each location, with their asset numbers;
- Navigate, which opens Google Maps directions as a top-level link (Referrer-Policy no-referrer, line 2596);
- "No pin on the record · ask on site" where there is no pin;
- a tick button per location.

HOW IT OPENS AN AREA. The script reads location.hash `#a<n>` (n = 0..13), opens that area and scrolls it into view. The overall bar and all other areas stay visible. The # part never reaches the server, as tested.

HOW IT LEARNS THE DAY FROM SERVER TIME.
- Every GET of ticks returns `now`, the server time. The card keeps `offset = Date.parse(now) - Date.now()`, measured at the midpoint of the request.
- `svcDay(ms) = new Date(ms + 2*3600e3).toISOString().slice(0,10)`. This is the Brisbane date of (time minus 8 h), so each day runs 08:00 to 08:00. Days are '2026-10-22' (Thu, labelled "if needed"), '2026-10-23', '2026-10-24' and '2026-10-25'.
- Before Thu 22 08:00 it opens on Friday, as the mock-up did (Thursday is "just in case"). After Mon 26 08:00 it stays on Sunday.
- Until the first reply arrives, the phone's clock is used. After that, the server's clock always wins.
- If the person has not picked a day themselves, the card moves on by itself at 08:00 and says so ("Now Saturday's service, from 08:00").
- Every tick carries its chosen day explicitly, so a tick queued offline that arrives after 08:00 still lands on the day it was made.

SHARED TICKS.
- It polls `GET <path>/ticks?since=<seq>` every 15 s while the page is visible, and straight away on load, on 'online', on becoming visible and after each successful post. Reads write nothing on the server.
- Known events are kept by id and applied in seq order.
- If the reply's seq is below the card's own cursor (the server recovered from a snapshot), the card resets to since=0 and refetches.
- It never reloads its own HTML: every GET /d/<t> is an open that rewrites cards.json and logs a line (lines 2581-2583).

STATE RULE, shared word for word with the main page. Events are taken in seq order, then this phone's unsent outbox in tap order.
- On done:true, if the row is not already done, record doneAt = tapped_at || at, and the name.
- On done:false, clear it.
- So "the time the reference was done" is the first tap since the last untick. A second phone ticking a row already done does not move the time.
- Percentages are counted by units (WC07's 20 weigh as 20) and rounded DOWN, so 256/257 shows 99%, never 100%.
- Each area shows "x of y locations · u of t units", its percentage and bar. When every row is done it shows "Area finished hh:mm", the latest doneAt of its rows.
- The header shows "u of 257 units serviced" and the overall percentage.
- Times are shown with Intl in Australia/Brisbane, 24-hour.

TICK AND UNDO.
- Tapping an open row makes an event `{id, row, day, done:true, tapped_at: new Date(Date.now()+offset).toISOString(), name}`.
- The id is 16 base64url characters from crypto.getRandomValues.
- A done row asks first (the mock-up's "Undo tick" button) and then queues done:false.
- An optional "Your name" box is stored on the phone and travels with each tick. The name is shown only on the edit link.

OUTBOX (offline-safe).
- Kept in localStorage at `gc500.svc1063.<token>.outbox`. Every read and write is wrapped in try/catch.
- All keys use the `gc500.svc1063.` prefix, because the card shares an origin with /e/ and /v/ and the main page keeps gc500.edit and gc500.view there. The card never reads those keys.
- Each event is shown straight away with a "waiting for signal" chip. The status line reads "No signal · 3 ticks waiting, they go when signal is back".
- Events are sent one at a time, in order, with `fetch(path+'/ticks', {method:'POST'})`:
  - 200 saved or already: removed from the outbox and merged.
  - 400 or 409: removed, with a plain message naming the row.
  - 507 with `full`: everything stops, the outbox is kept, and a banner says "ring Andrew".
  - Network failure, 5xx, 507 without `full`, or 413: retried after 5, 10, 20, 40 then 60 s.
  - 429: waits for Retry-After.
  - JSON 404 (withdrawn) or 410 (finished): final. ALL polling and posting stops, a banner shows the contact number, and the outbox is kept. At most one counted miss per phone, so phones behind one carrier address cannot lock each other out (30 misses in 5 min trips the limiter, lines 2362-2383).
  - Non-JSON 404 (a v5.87 rollback): "The service is being updated, your ticks are kept on this phone". It retries every 60 s. This is not counted by the limiter.

ALSO ON THE PAGE: a status line "Live · updated 21:14:05". A footer that reads "Track only: nothing here ticks the job record or changes a charge", with one tel: link to the TEAM lead. Dark mode as in the mock-up. A phone-first layout with 56 px tick targets. For tests only: `window.svc1063Day` and `window.svc1063State` are exposed as pure functions.

The base hash d5a0d777 matches, and the cited lines check out: 154, 159-160, 174-178, 2462/2528 (counted misses), 2568, 2581-2583, 2590-2600, 2776, 2809, 2944 (uncounted HTML 404), the machine blob routes 1204-1213, 1255-1266, 1296-1313 and 2914-2925, the STATUS.md v5.88 claim at line 2076, and the NEXT v10.61/v10.62 at line 3. The svcDay formula gives the right 08:00 Gold Coast boundaries, and nothing in the patch writes the record. But it has one blocker and four majors. (1) One public token has no write throttle and no way to clear it. I ran the scratchpad prototype locally with fake tokens: one address filled the tracker in 14.4 s, and after that every crew tick got 507 full. During the flood a record PUT went from 3 ms to 432 ms (p50), 933 ms at worst. (2) The typed crew name is a stored-XSS path to the edit key, because the main page has no CSP and the edit key sits in localStorage on the same origin. (3) Nights1022's own render() calls wipe the progress panel. (4) Re-posting with a missing or bad tracker quietly turns the tracker into a driver card, and phones then stop for good. I confirmed this on the prototype. (5) Offline unticks are applied in arrival order, so a late untick can wipe a newer tick from another crew. The probe scripts are /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fish/b3d08fad-688f-5986-9fd9-2f1442b3bb1a/scratchpad/svc589/review_flood.js and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fish/b3d08fad-688f-5986-9fd9-2f1442b3bb1a/scratchpad/svc589/review_baseline.js. Nothing in the repo was touched and nothing live was called.

problems.title: Anyone with one sheet can fill the tracker in about 15 s or fake its progress, there is no way to recover, and the flood slows the job record
problems.why: All 14 laminated sheets carry the same token. A photo of one sheet is enough. The wrong-key limiter never counts a right token (server.js 2354-2360), and the new route has no rate limit. Measured on the scratchpad prototype from one address with 16 connections: 5000 ticks saved in 14.4 s. Every crew tick after that got 507 {full:true}, which the card turns into 'everything stops, ring Andrew'. There is no edit-link route to void or clear ticks, and re-posting keeps them. A new card means a new token, so all 14 sheets would have to be reprinted mid-event. Every tick rewrites the whole tracker_ticks.json synchronously (writeWhole, lines 148-152), 1.13 MB by the cap. During the flood a record PUT took p50 432 ms and max 933 ms, against 3 ms and 10 ms at rest, and /health reached 241 ms. The same holder can tick or untick all 75 rows to show 100% or 0%, and can backdate tapped_at by up to 48 h, which feeds 'the time the reference was done' and the area finish time. Each GET since=0 after a flood returns about 0.7 MB uncompressed. Hourly snapshots of a full store, 96 kept plus 12 boot copies, can reach about 475 MB at the 20000 total cap. Separately, each GET /d/<t> (a card open) rewrites the whole cards.json and adds a log line with no limit (lines 2581-2583), and the page is now public.
problems.fix: 1. Rate-limit POST /d/<t>/ticks per address and per token, for example 20 a minute per address and a few hundred an hour per token, with 429 and Retry-After. 2. Cap events per row per day (for example 20) and refuse the excess, instead of shutting the whole tracker at 5000. 3. Add an edit-link-only void or reset route for ticks; it stays off the record. 4. Append one JSON line per tick (appendFileSync) instead of rewriting the whole file. 5. Paginate GET replies. 6. Throttle writing opens to disk for tracker cards. 7. Consider a short crew PIN typed once on each phone and checked on the server. 8. Ask Andrew whether the sheets are posted in public places or carried by crews.

problems.title: Typed crew name can run script on the edit link and steal the edit key
problems.why: name_given comes from anyone holding a sheet. The server only strips control characters and cuts it to 80 characters, enough for . The panel shows names on the edit link only. That page is served with no Content-Security-Policy (server.js 722-729: 'No Content-Security-Policy yet') and keeps the edit key in localStorage gc500.edit on the same origin (page 54399, 54401). If the panel draws the name into innerHTML unescaped, the edit key can be taken, and with it the whole record. The spec never asks for escaping or a hostile-name test. The existing report table does escape it (esc(r.name_given), page 39866).
problems.fix: Require esc() on every tick field the panel shows (name_given, row, day, times). Add test_page1063 checks: with a fixture name of '' and a quote and variant, window.__pwn stays undefined. Optionally narrow the server's name characters too.

problems.title: The panel vanishes whenever Kyle uses the run sheet
problems.why: The spec adds the panel by wrapping window.renderNights1022 (exported at page 88245, called from renderPass at 57527). But Nights1022 calls its own internal render() directly: on a night change (88143), after adding a request (88148), and after every tick or field change (88162-88163). Each call replaces pane.innerHTML (88104) and never passes through the wrapper, so #svc1063 is removed. The 20 s poll 'only #svc1063 is redrawn', so it then has nothing to draw into until the next renderPass.
problems.fix: Draw the panel into its own container outside the Nights1022 pane, or re-attach it with a MutationObserver on the pane, or have the poll re-insert it when it is missing. Add a test: tick a run-sheet unit box and switch nights; the panel is still there and the note field keeps its focus.

problems.title: A re-post with a missing or bad tracker quietly turns the tracker into a driver card, and every phone stops
problems.why: The spec adds `tracker` only when trackerConfig() comes back non-null. Otherwise the card object is rebuilt from the body without it (server.js 2777-2807). I confirmed this on the prototype: re-posting the same token with rows:[] answered 200, the card's tracker was gone, and /d/<t>/ticks then answered JSON 404 'this card has no tracker'. The card's rule treats any JSON 404 as final: all polling and posting stop and the outbox is kept. So one glitchy 'Update the tracker' stops every crew phone. A re-post made while rolled back to v5.87 drops the tracker the same way. A first post with a bad tracker makes a plain driver card that the page believes is a tracker.
problems.fix: On the server: answer 400 when the body has `tracker` but it does not validate, and 409 when a card that has a tracker is re-posted without one. Give each 404 a machine-readable code (withdrawn, no_tracker, not_ours). The card stops for good only on code 'withdrawn'.

problems.title: Offline unticks are applied in arrival order, so a late one wipes another crew's newer tick
problems.why: State is replayed in seq (arrival) order, and done:false clears the row. Example: phone A unticks WC06 offline at 02:00; phone B ticks WC06 online at 02:10 (seq n); A gets signal at 02:30 and its untick lands at seq n+1. WC06 now shows not done although B serviced it after A's undo. Similarly, 'doneAt = first done:true since the last untick' uses the first tick to arrive, not the earliest tap, so offline work gets the later time. The spec treats offline phones as a normal case (the outbox), so this will happen on event nights.
problems.fix: Make an untick name the tick id(s) it cancels (`undoes`, checked on the server against the same row and day). A row is done while any done:true it holds is not cancelled, and doneAt is the earliest uncancelled tapped_at (no later than its `at`). Add card test 12: two phones, one offline, untick versus a later tick.

problems.title: Recovery from a snapshot loses saved ticks silently and reuses seq numbers
problems.why: The tick store falls back to the hourly snapshot (step 3 with loadStore, lines 99-125). Up to an hour of ticks already answered 'saved' can be lost, and phones dropped them from their outboxes on that 200. New ticks then reuse seq numbers. The card's check, a reply seq below its cursor, misses the reset whenever the server's seq has grown past a phone's cursor before that phone polls. That phone then skips the reused range.
problems.fix: Return an `epoch` that changes whenever the store is loaded from a snapshot, in GET replies and in /api/ticks. On an epoch change the card starts again from since=0 and re-posts any id from its own log of sent ticks that the server no longer has. Sends are idempotent by id, so this is safe.

problems.title: Card address edge cases: a trailing slash, a second scan in an open tab, and 413 retried forever
problems.why: (a) /d/<t>/ is served 200 (line 2568 matches `\/?$`), but path + '/ticks' then becomes /d/<t>//ticks, which got the HTML 404 on the prototype. The card would show 'being updated' for good. (b) Scanning a second sheet while the card is already open changes only the # part, so the page does not reload; the spec reads location.hash at load only. (c) 413 is in the retry list, but the same body will never fit.
problems.fix: Build the path as location.pathname.replace(/\/+$/, ''). Listen for 'hashchange' and test it. Treat 413 like 400: drop it with a message. Cap the name box at 80 characters on the phone.

problems.title: Two trackers for one load, one shared cursor, and ticks hidden when a card is gone
problems.why: Make looks up an existing tracker by load through /api/ticks. Two editors pressing Make at once (or a lost reply plus a retry from another device) get two tokens for the same load, and /api/ticks gives no 'created' to choose between them. /api/ticks applies one `since` to every tracker, but each tracker counts seq on its own. The load filter skips cards that are withdrawn or pruned (c is null), so their ticks disappear from the panel.
problems.fix: On the server, refuse a second live tracker for a load when no token is given: 409 with the existing token. Return `created`. Take since per token (for example since[<token>]=n), or have the page poll by token. Keep orphaned ticks visible on the edit link.

problems.title: Day choice: a manual pick never lapses, and crews still working at 08:00 roll into the next day
problems.why: If someone picks a day, the card never moves on, so a tab left open from Friday can log Saturday's work against Friday. If no one picks, the card moves on at 08:00, and a crew finishing at 08:10 puts its last rows on the next day: the previous area never shows finished and the next day shows false early progress. The server accepts any configured day at any time, including future days.
problems.fix: Let a manual pick lapse at the next 08:00 boundary and show a loud 'You are on FRIDAY's service' banner. Offer a grace prompt after 08:00 if this phone ticked in the last hour. Refuse ticks on the server whose day is after the current service day (svcDay of server time). Confirm the grace rule with Andrew.

problems.title: A damaged tick file with no snapshot would stop the whole delivery service from starting
problems.why: The spec adopts the house rule (loadStore lines 109-113, process.exit). For a store that is 'purely just a track', that turns tracker_ticks.json into a single point of failure for the record, the edit link and the cards during event week. The risk window is the first hour after the first tick, before any hourly snapshot exists.
problems.fix: For ticks only: set the damaged file aside, start with an empty store, and report it on /health record_recovered and in the deploy banner. Or take a snapshot straight after the first tick is written.

problems.title: The contact must go to the server as `phone`, not `mobile`
problems.why: The spec says contact is the TEAM lead's {name, mobile}. The server keeps only contact.name and contact.phone (server.js 2785-2786). makeDropCard maps it as {name: lead.name, phone: lead.mobile} (page 39258). Built as written, the finished page has no tel: link.
problems.fix: Send contact: {name: lead.name, phone: lead.mobile || ''}. Add the check to test_page1063 #1.

problems.title: Card routes look tokens up without hasOwnProperty, a problem already in v5.87
problems.why: 'propertyIsEnumerable' is 20 characters and passes CARD_TOKEN_RE (line 140), and cards['propertyIsEnumerable'] is a function. On the prototype, GET /d/propertyIsEnumerable answered 200 with an empty body. It is not counted, logs a 'card open' and rewrites cards.json (lines 2581-2583), so anyone can force cards.json rewrites without any token. The new /ticks route repeats the pattern (404, not counted).
problems.fix: Use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(cards, token) in the new route. Fix the three existing /d/ routes and the token reuse check at 2776 in the same release.

problems.title: Printed sheets and the rules: twin-steer short form, the QR citation, and line references
problems.why: (a) v10.53 WORDING.md line 35 says the short form is 'printed on every page of every print-out', but the sheet footer list leaves it out. (b) AGENTS.md lines 149-150 literally say QR codes 'always use the view link'; the spec cites line 148 for 'never /v/'. The drop-card QRs are the real precedent. (c) The mock-up rule is AGENTS.md line 200, not 198, and /health starts at server.js 2402, not 2405.
problems.fix: Either print the twin-steer short form on each sheet or get Andrew's word that crew servicing sheets are exempt. Cite the drop-card precedent for /d/ QRs. Correct the line numbers.

problems.title: Coverage and data freshness: no waste tanks, asset numbers frozen in the page build, and a README line that conflicts with the rules
problems.why: areas13.json holds 257 units: 234 FWF, 4 accessible, 2 FWF trailers and 17 blocks (I checked all 75 rows). There are no duplicate refs and every ref passes TICK_ROW_RE. The 6 waste tanks Event Portables service (AGENTS.md line 223: 6 x 3 = 18) are not tracked. Asset numbers and pins are frozen into the page build, so a mid-event swap like WC48/WC53 needs a page release before the card shows it. Phones holding the old HTML are never told the rows changed. The draft README says the Thursday count 'can follow what was actually done' from ticks, which conflicts with AGENTS.md line 223 'Scans and ticks never change either figure'.
problems.fix: Ask Andrew whether the waste tanks belong on the tracker. Build the asset numbers and pins from the live record when 'Update the tracker' is pressed, keeping his area grouping and showing the difference first. Add a config stamp to GET replies so the card shows 'tracker updated, reload'. Strike the README line, or note that only Andrew's word changes the count.

problems.title: Test steps on the live service write to it
problems.why: The TEST tracker writes to the live cards.json and tracker_ticks.json, and its ticks count toward the 20000 total cap and appear on the view link for good. AGENTS.md line 151 says tests only read the live service. The spec does put this step under Andrew's 'Upload' (c), which is right, but the residue is not addressed.
